cards.title: Accops for Government: Zero Trust Reference Architecture, Seven Integrated Components (2026 V2)
cards.key_problem: A government organisation hardening its IT needs one Zero Trust design covering private application access, identity, isolated desktops, internet browsing, cross-network file transfer, remote IT support and endpoints - replacing VPNs, NAC, WAF and separate access portals rather than bolting on seven point products.
key_outcomes: Seven 'off the shelf' components in one reference architecture: ZTNA, HyID (MFA/SSO/IAM), VDI Suite, Remote Browser Isolation, AirBridge, Huddle and HyDesk thin clients - each with capabilities, a reference architecture diagram and use cases

ZTNA replaces VPN with identity- and application-level access: Layer 7 reverse proxy, Layer 4 tunnelling, device posture, context policies, clientless or agent access, DLP (copy-paste, screenshot, screen-recording blocks) and support for external QRNG for post-quantum cryptography
Web application protection against OWASP Top 10, OWASP Top 20 automated threats and SANS Top 25

Four ZTNA deployment options - on-premises or cloud, each direct-connect or reverse-connect via Edge and App Connectors with no inbound firewall ports - and two models: self-hosted or ZTNA-as-a-service
HyID: OTP, push, biometrics, hardware tokens, QR passwordless login, FIDO and Windows Hello, SAML 2.0/OAuth SSO, RADIUS connectors, impossible-travel detection, device binding, SIEM integration
VDI for developers, auditors, external vendors (time-bound sandboxes with auto-reset) and privileged admins, with session recording, USB/screen-capture blocking and non-persistent desktops

Remote Browser Isolation streams only pixels; AirBridge moves files between isolated networks with multi-engine AV scanning and Content Disarm and Reconstruction; Huddle gives on-premise remote support that works in air-gapped networks
cards.brief: A nine-page, component-by-component solution document written as a proposal for 'Government Organisations'. Each of the seven components gets a product overview, key capabilities, a reference architecture diagram and a use-case list. ZTNA is the most detailed section (deployment topologies, flexible model, seven use cases including VPN replacement and consolidating VPN/NAC/WAF/portals). The VDI section is the one to point at for privileged access, auditor and third-party developer scenarios; Browser Isolation plus AirBridge covers internet-to-internal separation; Huddle and HyDesk cover remote support and endpoint replacement. No customers, prices or statistics are cited. Its content is the same as the SharePoint 'Accops Solutions for Govt. V1 '26' (differences are typesetting and a few words).
cards.use_for: Send to a government, PSU or public-sector prospect - or attach to a tender/RFP response - when they need the full architecture in one document: VPN replacement with ZTNA, air-gapped or isolated networks, secure file transfer between networks, internet isolation, or thin-client rollouts. This is the public, sendable edition.
